_transcription: Chemistry = pages p18-p32 (the section restarts its own page numbering at 1). Printed numbers 1-15, one question per page, no continuation pages. Numbers checked unbroken 1..15 against the 'N. Question N' headings. Q6's reaction (tert-butyl bromide + hydroxide in ethanol), Q9's reaction scheme and Q10's four amines are drawings that type exactly, so they are typed and not cropped. Stem figures: Q8 (p25 TLC plate), Q12 (p29 four process diagrams). Picture options: Q7 (p24, stereo drawings of tetramethyl-1,3-dioxanes, described bond by bond), Q9 (p26, each option a pair of structures X and P, typed as formula and name).

rows.subtopic: Bonding in Some Homonuclear Diatomic Molecules
rows.text: Which one of the following molecules shows an increase in bond order after loss of an electron from the highest occupied molecular orbital?

Metal-ligand \(\pi\)-bond formation in \(\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}\) and \(\mathrm{[MnO_4]^-}\) requires electron-pair donation between metal and ligand orbitals. Which one of the following represents the direction of electron-pair donation?
options: \(\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}\): metal orbital \(\rightarrow\) ligand orbital; \(\mathrm{[MnO_4]^-}\): ligand orbital \(\rightarrow\) metal orbital
\(\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}\): ligand orbital \(\rightarrow\) metal orbital; \(\mathrm{[MnO_4]^-}\): ligand orbital \(\rightarrow\) metal orbital
\(\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}\): metal orbital \(\rightarrow\) ligand orbital; \(\mathrm{[MnO_4]^-}\): metal orbital \(\rightarrow\) ligand orbital
\(\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}\): ligand orbital \(\rightarrow\) metal orbital; \(\mathrm{[MnO_4]^-}\): metal orbital \(\rightarrow\) ligand orbital

rows.text: What is the order of bond energy between \(\mathrm{C{=}S}\) & \(\mathrm{C{=}Te}\), and between \(\mathrm{Cl{-}Cl}\) & \(\mathrm{F{-}F}\)?

Which one is an INCORRECT statement with regard to the following reaction?

\(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C{-}Br + {}^-OH \xrightarrow{CH_3CH_2OH} (CH_3)_3C{-}OH + Br^-}\)
options: The reaction rate decreases upon changing the solvent from ethyl alcohol to 1:1 mixture of ethyl alcohol and water.
The reaction rate does not change upon increasing the concentration of hydroxide ion.
The rate determining step is the dissociation of tert-butylbromide.
The reaction rate is proportional to the concentration of tert-butylbromide.

rows.text: Consider the following silica-gel based thin-layer chromatogram of compounds **A** and **B**. Which one of the following statements is correct?

rows.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
rows.text:
What are **X** and **P** in the following reaction sequence?

\(\mathrm{\mathit{o}\text{-}C_6H_4(CHO)(CDO) \xrightarrow[\Delta]{Conc.\ NaOH} \mathbf{X} \xrightarrow{HCl\ gas\ (excess)} \mathbf{P}}\)

What is the order of \(\mathrm{p}K_b\) for the following molecules in an aqueous medium?

P: \(\mathrm{PhCH_2NH_2}\)
Q: \(\mathrm{PhNHCH_3}\)
R: \(\mathrm{PhN(CH_3)_2}\)
S: \(\mathrm{PhNH_2}\)

100 mL of 1.0 M aqueous NaOH solution was diluted to 1.0 L by adding water. Half of this solution was discarded. A new 100 mL of 0.5 M aqueous NaOH solution was added to the remaining solution. What is the concentration of the final aqueous NaOH solution?

An ideal gas goes through a reversible isothermal expansion (solid line) followed by a reversible adiabatic expansion (dashed line). Which of the following diagram(s) closely depict(s) the entire process?

figure.note: Four diagrams. (i) P against V: a solid curve falling, then a dashed curve continuing to fall more steeply to larger V. (ii) T against V: a solid horizontal line, then a dashed curve rising steeply to larger V. (iii) P against T: a dashed curve rising from low T and low P to meet a solid vertical line at higher T that runs upward. (iv) P against 1/V: a solid straight line rising from near the origin to a peak, then a dashed curve falling as 1/V increases further.

rows.text: What is the ratio of the velocity of an electron in the fourth orbit of \(\mathrm{Be^{3+}}\) to the velocity of the electron in the second orbit of \(\mathrm{He^+}\)?

For two pure volatile liquids **X** and **Y**, attractive intermolecular interactions of both **X-X** and **Y-Y** are weaker than those of **X-Y**. The total vapour pressure of an equimolar solution of **X** and **Y** is \(p_{\text{total}}\). The vapour pressure of pure **X** and pure **Y** are \(p^0_{\mathbf{X}}\) and \(p^0_{\mathbf{Y}}\), respectively. Which one of the following relations is correct?

rows.subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
rows.text: The rate constant of a reaction at 600 K with an activation energy of 191.47 kJ \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\) is \(5.0 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\). What is the temperature at which the half-life of the reaction becomes 152 s? [Consider pre-exponential factor and activation energy to be independent of temperature. R = 8.314 J \(\mathrm{K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}\)]
